version.changelog:
Furry Art Generator skill initial release:

- Generate furry art images from text descriptions using the Neta talesofai API.
- Supports image options: size (`portrait`, `landscape`, `square`, `tall`) and style (`anime`, `cinematic`, `realistic`).
- Returns a direct image URL instantly.
- Simple CLI usage with Node.js.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: furry-art-skill
Version: 1.0.0

The script `furryart.js` accesses the local filesystem to read sensitive `.env` files from the user's home directory (specifically `~/.openclaw/workspace/.env` and `~/developer/clawhouse/.env`) to retrieve an API token. While this is plausibly needed for the stated purpose of authenticating with the Neta talesofai API (`api.talesofai.cn`), direct reading of shared environment files that may contain other unrelated secrets is a risky capability. The script otherwise appears to function as a legitimate client for the image generation service.

llm.summary: The skill mostly does what it says (submit prompts to the talesofai API) but there are inconsistencies and privacy-surprising behaviors (undeclared required token and reading user .env files) that warrant caution.

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose (generate images via the Neta/talesofai API) matches the code's network activity. However, the registry metadata lists no required environment variables, while the code and README clearly require a NETA_TOKEN credential. That mismatch is an incoherence in the manifest.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and README instruct running node furryart.js which is consistent, but the implementation reads secrets from ~/.openclaw/workspace/.env and ~/developer/clawhouse/.env (and process.env.NETA_TOKEN). Reading those user-home files is not obvious from the top-level metadata and is a privacy/scope extension: the script reads arbitrary files in the user's home to locate a token (it only extracts NETA_TOKEN, but it still opens those files).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (instruction-only plus a single JS file). That lowers install risk — nothing is downloaded or executed from an external installer by the registry. The code is included in the bundle, so installation just places these files locally (no third-party fetch at install time).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The code requires a secret (NETA_TOKEN) to call the external API, which is reasonable for the stated purpose. But the registry metadata did not declare this required environment variable. The script also looks for tokens in two specific dotfile locations in the user home; this increases the chance of accidentally using or exposing a token from an unexpected source. There are no other unrelated credentials requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request permanent presence (always: false) and does not modify other skills or system-wide configs. It only runs as a local Node script and does network calls to the API endpoints in the code.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Key points before installing: (1) The skill needs a NETA_TOKEN even though the registry metadata doesn't declare it — provide it via --token or the NETA_TOKEN environment variable to avoid the script scanning your home .env files. (2) The script will attempt to read ~/.openclaw/workspace/.env and ~/developer/clawhouse/.env to find NETA_TOKEN; inspect those files first (they may contain other secrets) or avoid placing tokens there. (3) Network calls go to https://api.talesofai.cn — consider whether you trust that external service and review its privacy/retention and content-moderation policies. (4) Because code is included, you can open furryart.js (already present) to review what it does (it only posts JSON and polls for an image URL, extracting NETA_TOKEN with a regex). (5) If you have sensitive environment files, run this in an isolated environment or explicitly pass --token or NETA_TOKEN to control which credential is used. (6) The manifest inconsistency (undeclared required env) is a red flag for sloppy packaging; request the author to declare NETA_TOKEN in requires.env or fix the SKILL.md/registry before trusting it widely.
